title: GRC Fundamentals — Sample Set
description: Entry-level check across GRC foundations, risk management, controls, TPRM, ISO 27001, audit evidence and privacy. Low-stakes practice; answers are revealed only after submit.

options: Aligning governance, risk management and compliance so the organisation meets objectives while staying within obligations
Replacing internal audit with automated dashboards
questions.question: What is the primary purpose of Governance, Risk and Compliance (GRC)?
questions.rationale: GRC integrates governance structures, risk processes and compliance obligations so risk-taking stays aligned with strategy — it does not eliminate risk.

questions.question: Which artefact formally expresses how much risk an organisation is willing to take?
questions.rationale: The risk appetite statement, approved by governance, sets boundaries; the register tracks individual risks against it.

questions.question: What is the correct order of the core risk management lifecycle?
questions.rationale: Risks must be identified, then assessed (likelihood × impact), treated per appetite, then continuously monitored.

options: A control that stops an unwanted event before it happens
A control that fixes data after a breach
A report sent to regulators each quarter
A backup restored during disaster recovery
questions.question: Which BEST describes a preventive control?
questions.rationale: Preventive controls (e.g. MFA, segregation of duties) act before an event; detective controls find it, corrective controls fix it.

options: Access to sensitive data, criticality of the service, and substitutability
questions.question: What should drive inherent-risk tiering of a third party in TPRM?
questions.rationale: Tiering reflects what the vendor can impact (data, critical operations) and how hard it is to replace — not price or paperwork alone.

options: An independent auditor's opinion on the operating effectiveness of a service organisation's controls
questions.question: In a vendor review, what does a SOC 2 Type II report give you?
questions.rationale: SOC 2 Type II is an independent attestation over a period, covering operating effectiveness — stronger than self-attestations or point-in-time Type I.

options: Scope, leadership accountability, risk assessment, objectives and documented processes for operating them
questions.question: Under ISO/IEC 27001:2022, what must an ISMS include at minimum?
questions.rationale: Clause 4–10 requires defined scope, leadership, risk assessment/treatment, objectives, resources, documented processes and continual improvement.

options: Recording which Annex A controls apply (with justifications for inclusions and exclusions) and how they are implemented
questions.question: What is the Statement of Applicability (SoA) in ISO 27001?
questions.rationale: The SoA maps each Annex A control to in/out-of-scope with justification plus implementation status — a mandatory audit artefact.

options: Whether evidence is sufficient, relevant and reliable to support the control conclusion
How long the auditee has worked at the company
questions.question: During control testing, what is the auditor actually judging about evidence?
questions.rationale: Audit conclusions stand on evidence that is sufficient (enough), relevant (on-point) and reliable (trustworthy source).

options: Collect as much personal data as possible for future use
Process only the personal data that is adequate, relevant and limited to the stated purpose
Keep personal data forever to train models
Share personal data with any partner to reduce storage cost
questions.question: What does the data-minimisation principle require?
questions.rationale: Data minimisation (GDPR Art. 5, mirrored in global privacy regimes) limits collection and retention to what the purpose needs.
